tasks.title: Implement GFM Markdown table renderer
tasks.description: Create a MarkdownRenderer class in the CsvToMarkdown library that accepts an IEnumerable of string arrays (rows) and produces a GFM-style pipe table string with a header row, separator row, body rows, and a trailing footer line reporting the data row count.

tasks.title: Implement public CsvConverter API
tasks.description: Create a public CsvConverter class that wires CsvParser and MarkdownRenderer together. It should accept an input CSV file path and an optional output path, defaulting to same directory as input with .md extension, and write the rendered Markdown to disk.

tasks.title: Add renderer and integration tests with artifacts
tasks.description: Write xUnit tests for MarkdownRenderer (minimal table, multi-row, empty field, quoted comma edge case) and end-to-end integration tests for CsvConverter. All tests must write actual .md output to artifacts/test-output/ so humans can inspect them after dotnet test.

tasks.title: Implement CLI entry point
tasks.description: Update Program.cs in CsvToMarkdown.Cli to accept a CSV file path as a command-line argument, invoke CsvConverter, and report success or usage errors to stdout/stderr with a non-zero exit code on failure.

tasks.title: Add streaming large-file test
tasks.description: Add a test (or inline justification in code) that verifies the conversion pipeline does not load the entire CSV into memory at once. Generate a file with many rows in the test and assert correct row count in output footer.

tasks.title: Update README with artifact path and usage
tasks.description: Add a README.md at the repo root documenting how to run the CLI, how to run dotnet test, where artifact .md outputs are written (artifacts/test-output/), and how to refresh golden files when output changes intentionally.

tasks.title: Create ASP.NET Core Web API project
tasks.description: Add a new ASP.NET Core minimal API project (CsvToMarkdown.Api) to the solution, referencing the CsvToMarkdown library. Wire it into the .slnx and configure it for net10.0 with Swagger/OpenAPI enabled.

tasks.title: Implement in-memory job store
tasks.description: Define a Job model (id, status enum, result bytes, error) and an IJobStore interface with InMemoryJobStore implementation using a thread-safe dictionary. Register it as a singleton in the DI container.

tasks.title: Implement upload endpoint
tasks.description: Add POST /jobs accepting multipart/form-data with a CSV file. Queue a background Task that runs CsvConverter, storing the result in IJobStore. Return 202 Accepted with the job id and initial status immediately without blocking.

tasks.title: Implement status and download endpoints
tasks.description: Add GET /jobs/{id} returning JSON with job id and status (queued/running/succeeded/failed plus optional error summary). Add GET /jobs/{id}/result returning the Markdown file as text/markdown when succeeded, or 404/409 otherwise.

tasks.title: Write API integration tests
tasks.description: Add an xUnit test project (CsvToMarkdown.Api.Tests) using WebApplicationFactory. Cover upload-poll-download for a small edge-case CSV and for a 10k-row CSV. Assert status transitions, footer row count, and that incomplete jobs do not return a result. Persist input CSV and output .md to artifacts/test-output/.

tasks.title: Update README with API documentation
tasks.description: Extend README.md with API usage (curl examples for upload, status, download), Swagger URL, documented exit/error contracts, and how to run the API tests. Note the artifact folder entries added by the API test suite.

## Next Task: Create ASP.NET Core Web API Project (Task 7)

### What needs to be done and why it matters

All Epic 2 work depends on having a runnable ASP.NET Core Web API project in the solution. This task establishes the project skeleton: a new project, solution reference, library dependency, and Swagger/OpenAPI scaffolding. Nothing else (job store, endpoints, tests) can be built until this foundation exists.

### Implementation guidance

1. **Create the project** using the `dotnet new webapi` template:
   - Project name: `CsvToMarkdown.Api`
   - Target path: `src/CsvToMarkdown.Api/`
   - Target framework: `net10.0`
   - Use minimal API style (not controllers) to match the rest of the solution's lean footprint.
   - Include OpenAPI/Swagger support (the template includes it by default for `webapi`).

2. **Add project reference** to the core library:
   - `src/CsvToMarkdown.Api/CsvToMarkdown.Api.csproj` must reference `../CsvToMarkdown/CsvToMarkdown.csproj`.

3. **Wire into the solution**:
   - Add the new project to `CsvToMarkdown.slnx` with `dotnet sln add`.

4. **Confirm Swagger is enabled**:
   - The generated `Program.cs` should call `builder.Services.AddOpenApi()` (or the Swashbuckle equivalent for net10), and map `/openapi/v1.json` (or `/swagger`) in development mode.
   - Keep the default weather-forecast sample endpoint removed; replace with a placeholder comment or a simple health-check route (`GET /health` returning `200 OK`) to verify the host starts.

5. **Project file essentials**:
   - `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>`
   - `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`
   - `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`

### Testing steps

1. Run `dotnet build` from the repo root - all projects (library, CLI, API, tests) must compile with no errors.
2. Run `dotnet run --project src/CsvToMarkdown.Api` and confirm the host starts and listens (port logged to stdout).
3. Hit `GET /health` (or the Swagger JSON endpoint) with `curl` and verify a `200` response.
4. Run `dotnet test` - existing tests must still pass; no regressions introduced.

### Acceptance criteria

- `src/CsvToMarkdown.Api/CsvToMarkdown.Api.csproj` exists, targets `net10.0`, and references the `CsvToMarkdown` library.
- The project is registered in `CsvToMarkdown.slnx`.
- `dotnet build` succeeds with zero errors from the repo root.
- `dotnet run --project src/CsvToMarkdown.Api` starts without runtime errors.
- At least one reachable route (e.g., `GET /health`) returns `200 OK`.
- `dotnet test` continues to pass all existing tests.
